rv.q: What’s most impressive about “Triumph” is how clear-eyed it is.

It’s not hard to discern the parallels in this 20-minute work being presented free by the Public (that is, if you can score tickets) and receiving a simultaneous production at London’s Almeida Theatre.

Churchill’s central argument—that the enablement of authoritarianism throughout history has gotten us to where we are today—is undoubtedly important, but hardly revolutionary to an audience that’s already card-carrying members of the #Resistance.

cn.t: Critics praise Caryl Churchill's sharp 20-minute play "Triumph," with Annaleigh Ashford earning acclaim as a press secretary delivering grandiose claims. The production brilliantly draws parallels between ancient Roman history and contemporary politics.

vr.q: Overall, this piece feels more like a sketch from a journal entry than anything else, or a political comic strip on stage.
